items.title: Anthropic falls below IPO price as Nvidia gives back gains
items.summary: In this edition of Sozzi Unleashed: At The Close, Brian Sozzi sorts through "reality trading" as Nvidia slides nearly 7% after Monday's 31% surge and Anthropic falls below its $83 IPO price less than a week after the biggest offering in history. GCG Advisory Partners' Bill Gunderson makes the case that Nvidia is the cheapest growth stock in the market at nine times forward earnings and names Nvidia and Eli Lilly as his top picks for 2027. Brian breaks down Dell's blowout quarter and $132 billion AI backlog, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to explain the company's raised outlook, why it refuses to finance neoclouds, and whether server margins have peaked. Brian closes by arguing the AI trade is reaching consumers' wallets, pointing to Best Buy's strongest comparable sales growth in five years.

items.title: Why Nvidia is 'bar none' the 'cheapest growth stock in the market'

items.title: Why the Jensen Huang rally faded so quickly
items.summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including why Monday's Jensen Huang rally faded within a day, what teeth the congressional hearings and board investigation can have given why he was reinstated, and whether the market is sniffing out a peak in the AI CapEx cycle the way it has in past build-outs. The panel debates what the VIX and implied correlations say about last week's selloff, why small caps lagged even in the rally, how a Fed rate hike changes the cost of capital for data center projects, and why investors now have to "take out the pencil" and discount AI earnings years out, before closing with a lighter debate on whether anyone would watch the Super Bowl in an IMAX theater.

items.summary: Technology firms once again tumbled Wednesday as the euphoria that greeted the return of Nvidia's Jensen Huang was washed away by the now-common panic and uncertainty over the AI boom.He said "professional investors (were) apparently using the opening provided by the Jensen Huang comeback to unload technology exposure rather than rebuild it".
